title: Geometric irreducibility and purely transcendental extensions
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Geometric irreducibility of an extension $L/F$ means geometric irreducibility of the $F$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. If $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible, then for every finite algebraically independent family $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ over $K$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree], the extension $K(t_1,\ldots,t_r)/k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is geometrically irreducible. Here adjoining the variables means forming successive rational function fields [def-weil-rational-function-field], and $r=0$ is allowed. Conversely, if $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible for one indeterminate $t$ over $K$, then $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: We use the geometric definition literally: the affine fibre-product formula identifies the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ along $\operatorname{Spec}F'\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_F F')$. Thus $L/F$ is geometrically irreducible exactly when these spectra are nonempty and irreducible for all field extensions $F'/F$. It suffices first to prove the two implications for the formal variable $t$; a transcendental element gives the same fraction field by evaluation, since no nonzero polynomial vanishes at it.

Put $R=K\otimes_k k(t)$ and $S_0=k[T]\setminus\{0\}$. There is a $K$-algebra isomorphism $R\cong S_0^{-1}K[T]$ sending $a\otimes f(t)/g(t)$ to $af(T)/g(T)$. Its inverse sends $h(T)/g(T)$ to $\sum_i h_i\otimes t^i/g(t)$, where $h=\sum_i h_iT^i$. The tensor universal property verifies the first map; the fraction relation verifies the second, and the two formulas compose to the identity. Under this identification, inverting in $R$ the images of all nonzero polynomials of $K[T]$ gives $K(t)$: every fraction is $h/g$ with $g\ne0$, and the two successive denominator sets together invert exactly these polynomials. These are explicit fraction constructions, valid over any field $k$ and any extension $K$.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward proof: K(t) is a localization of K tensor_k k(t); explicit fraction calculation supplying that sentence

proof.text: Assume $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible and let $F/k(t)$ be any field extension. Set $A=K\otimes_k F$ and $B=K(t)\otimes_{k(t)}F$. The spectrum of $A$ is irreducible by step 1, since $F$ is also a field extension of $k$. Give $A$ the $R$-algebra map $a\otimes v\mapsto a\otimes v$. The localization base-change lemma applied to $R\to K(t)$ shows that $A\otimes_R K(t)$ is a localization of $A$. This ring is isomorphic to $B$: send $(a\otimes f)\otimes u$ to $au\otimes f$, with inverse $u\otimes f\mapsto(1\otimes f)\otimes u$. Balancing over $R$ and over $k(t)$ verifies these maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors. Finally $B\ne0$ by the nonzero-vector-space tensor theorem over the field $k(t)$, since both $K(t)$ and $F$ are nonzero vector spaces. No reducedness of $A$ or $B$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward proof, localization after scalar extension; Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization)

proof.text: Write $B=M^{-1}A$ as in step 3. We check irreducibility rather than assuming that every nonempty subspace of an irreducible space is irreducible. By the component/minimal-prime theorem, irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ gives a unique minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ and $V(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $B\ne0$, apply existence of a minimal prime over the proper ideal $(0)$ in $B$ to get a point $\mathfrak q$ of its spectrum. The localization-spectrum theorem gives $\mathfrak q\cap A$ disjoint from $M$. Every prime of $A$ contains a minimal prime, hence contains $\mathfrak p$; in particular $\mathfrak p\cap M=\varnothing$. The same localization theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $D=\{\mathfrak r:\mathfrak r\cap M=\varnothing\}$, which therefore contains $\mathfrak p$. Every closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $\mathfrak p$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$: if it is $V(I)$ then $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and every prime contains $I$. Consequently every relatively closed subset of $D$ containing $\mathfrak p$ is $D$. In any cover of $D$ by two relatively closed subsets, one contains $\mathfrak p$ and is therefore $D$. Thus $D$ is nonempty and irreducible, as required. Since $F/k(t)$ was arbitrary, $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward proof: irreducibility of the localization; expanded using Tags 00ES, 00E0 and 00E3

proof.text: For a family $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ algebraically independent over $K$, put $K_i=K(t_1,\ldots,t_i)$ and $k_i=k(t_1,\ldots,t_i)$. The induction claim is that $K_i/k_i$ is geometrically irreducible for $0\le i\le r$. The base case $i=0$ is the hypothesis. Algebraic independence implies that $t_{i+1}$ is transcendental over $K_i$: a polynomial relation over $K_i$ could be multiplied by a common nonzero polynomial denominator to give a nonzero polynomial relation over $K$ among the first $i+1$ variables. Apply the one-variable forward implication of steps 1--4 to $K_i/k_i$ to obtain the next case. This proves the finite-family assertion, including the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0G31, forward implication, iterated finitely many times; Tag 0G32 (lemma-geometrically-irreducible-add-transcendental), fraction-field interpretation

proof.text: For the converse assume $K(t)/k(t)$ geometrically irreducible, and fix any field extension $k'/k$. Put $C=K\otimes_k k'$, $D=K(t)\otimes_k k'$ and $E=k(t)\otimes_k k'$. The fraction calculation of step 2, with $K$ replaced by $k'$ and the tensor factors interchanged, identifies $E$ with $S_0^{-1}k'[T]$. Its natural map $i:E\to k'(t)$ is injective: the coefficient map $k[T]\to k'[T]$ is injective, so every denominator from $S_0$ is nonzero in the polynomial domain $k'[T]$; a fraction $h/g$ that vanishes in the fraction field must have $h=0$ and was already zero in the localization. This proves the needed injection without identifying $E$ with all of $k'(t)$.

source.place: Tag 0G31, converse proof: details omitted for the injective tensor map, first fraction calculation

proof.text: Every module over a field is flat by the cited field-flatness statement. Tensor the injective $k$-linear map $K\hookrightarrow K(t)$ with the flat $k$-module $k'$; flat tensor exactness gives an injection $C\hookrightarrow D$. There is a $k(t)$-algebra isomorphism $D\cong K(t)\otimes_{k(t)}E$: the map back sends $u\otimes(v\otimes a)$ to $uv\otimes a$ and its inverse sends $u\otimes a$ to $u\otimes(1\otimes a)$, as checked by the tensor balancing relations. Now tensor the injection $i:E\hookrightarrow k'(t)$ from step 6 over $k(t)$ with the flat $k(t)$-module $K(t)$. Flat tensor exactness gives a second injection $D\hookrightarrow B'=K(t)\otimes_{k(t)}k'(t)$. Their composite $C\hookrightarrow B'$ sends $a\otimes b$ to $a\otimes b$. This supplies the exact omitted injectivity assertion in Tag 0G31 for arbitrary, including inseparable, $k'/k$.

source.place: Tag 0G31, converse proof: details omitted for injectivity, supplied using Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), equivalence (1)--(2)

proof.text: Since $k'(t)/k(t)$ is a field extension, the hypothesis and the affine base-change formula imply that $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is irreducible. For the injection $C\hookrightarrow B'$ of step 7, the injective-minimal-prime lifting theorem hits every minimal prime of $C$; the dense-range criterion therefore says that $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ has dense image. Its continuity is functoriality of the affine spectrum. To check the conclusion explicitly, if $\operatorname{Spec}C=Z_1\cup Z_2$ is a closed cover, inverse images give a closed cover of the irreducible source, so one inverse image is the whole source. Its dense image lies in the corresponding closed $Z_i$, forcing $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The target is nonempty since the source is nonempty. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is irreducible for every $k'/k$, which is precisely geometric irreducibility of $K/k$.
